pages.text: There is no iron ore block. There is $(bold)hematite$(), which is what iron ore is called in the ground. Geolosys names every deposit after its mineral, and the mineral tells you the metal.$(br2)$(bold)Hematite, Limonite$() = iron$(br)$(bold)Malachite, Azurite$() = copper$(br)$(bold)Sphalerite$() = zinc$(br)$(bold)Cassiterite, Teallite$() = tin

$(bold)Galena$() = lead, with silver in it$(br)$(bold)Bauxite$() = aluminum$(br)$(bold)Cinnabar$() = redstone$(br)$(bold)Kimberlite$() = diamond$(br)$(bold)Beryl$() = emerald$(br)$(bold)Lignite, Bituminous, Anthracite$() = coal, soft to hard$(br)$(bold)Platinum, Gold, Lapis, Quartz$() are themselves.

Mine a mineral and you get a $(bold)cluster$() of its metal, never a raw ore. Smelt it, or crush and wash it in Create for more: washed galena also gives silver, washed nickel a little platinum.$(br2)Uranium is not in this world. Anything else you dig up, EMI knows a use for.

$(bold)Tin$(): bronze, Ironworks tools, buckets, lanterns$(br)$(bold)Lead$(): musket and cannon shot$(br)$(bold)Nickel$(): constantan, invar$(br)$(bold)Silver$(): electrum$(br)$(bold)Aluminum$(): balloon sheets$(br)$(bold)Platinum$(): a quicker precision mechanism$(br2)Alloys mix in a heated basin. Smiths and clerics buy the metals for emeralds, and Spartan Weaponry arms you with all of them.
